issues.legal_issue: A voluntary and accepted division of some family property binds the parties even when other property remains undivided.
material_facts: The family members voluntarily referred their dispute over shares and division of property to arbitrators.
The parties accepted the decision allocating shares and accepted later divisions made in stages.
The parties took possession of properties allotted to them.
The court found that the allegation that consent was obtained by coercion or undue influence had not been proved.
issues.conclusion: The divisions already made and accepted were binding; the properties actually allotted and possessed belonged individually to their recipients, while the remaining property was held in common and could be partitioned.
issues.legal_principle: Under Hindu law, family members may divide some family properties while leaving others undivided. An agreement to refer the division dispute severs joint-family status; accepted divisions acted upon by taking possession establish individual ownership of the allotted properties, with undivided properties thereafter held as tenants-in-common.

rule.if: partition_proceeding and voluntary_family_reference and accepted_property_divisions and possession_taken and not consent_vitiated

predicates.partition_proceeding: The court is deciding a proceeding seeking partition of family property.
predicates.voluntary_family_reference: Family members voluntarily referred their dispute over shares or division to persons chosen to resolve it.
predicates.accepted_property_divisions: The family members accepted divisions of particular properties made under the agreed process.
predicates.possession_taken: The recipients took possession of properties allotted to them.
predicates.consent_vitiated: The consent to the reference or divisions was obtained through a legally vitiating circumstance.

issues.definition: When a partition proceeding concerns property divided voluntarily and accepted by the family members, and the allotted property was possessed without vitiated consent, the completed divisions bind them and the remaining property is held in common.

issues.legal_issue: Revocation of authority to continue an arbitration does not undo divisions that the parties had already accepted and acted upon.
material_facts: The court revoked the arbitrators’ authority after an arbitrator became unwilling to continue.
Before revocation, the parties had accepted and acted upon divisions of several properties made in stages.
The arbitrators had not completed the division of all the property.
issues.conclusion: Revocation of the reference did not nullify the accepted divisions already made; it left the remaining property to be divided.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 12(2) of the Arbitration Act, 1940, a court granting leave to revoke an arbitrator’s authority may order that the arbitration agreement cease to have effect for the referred difference. That does not vacate divisions already accepted and acted upon by the parties.

predicates.partition_proceeding: The court is deciding a proceeding seeking partition of family property after a division reference.
predicates.court_revoked_reference: A court revoked the authority of the persons appointed to continue dividing the property.
predicates.accepted_divisions_acted_upon: The parties accepted and acted upon particular divisions before the authority was revoked.

issues.definition: In a partition proceeding, revocation of a division reference does not undo divisions the parties had already accepted and acted upon.

issues.legal_issue: A party may defend a suit by relying on a mutually agreed settlement that was voluntarily performed, without relying on the arbitration award as such.
material_facts: The parties accepted the arbitrators’ decisions and voluntarily acted on the resulting divisions.
A party later sued while disregarding those divisions.
The defence relied on the parties’ agreement to divide the property and their subsequent conduct, rather than seeking a decision on the existence, effect, or validity of an award.
issues.conclusion: The defence based on the mutually agreed and performed divisions was not barred by section 32 of the Arbitration Act, 1940.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 31(2), 32, and 33 of the Arbitration Act, 1940, address where and how questions concerning an arbitration agreement or award may be decided and restrict suits seeking decisions on an award or agreement. The Court did not decide the broader dispute over whether an unfiled award itself can be pleaded as a defence. It held that a defence based instead on a mutual settlement and acts performed under it is not barred by section 32. The Court discussed Muhammad Nawaz Khan v. Alam Khan, Babui S. K. Kuer v. B. N. Sinha, Sait Pamandass v. T. S. Manikyam Pillai, Bhimavarapu Venkatasubbauva v. Addanki Bapadu, Firm Gulzarimal Gheesdal v. Firm Rameshrhandra Radhyeshyam, Pamudurthi Suryanarayana Reddy v. Pamudurthi Venkata Reddi, and Rajamanickam Pillai v. Swaminatha Pillai, but expressly left the broader question undecided.

predicates.suit_ignores_performed_settlement: A party brought a suit disregarding a settlement that had already been carried out.
predicates.parties_voluntarily_accepted_and_perform: The parties voluntarily accepted a division arrangement and performed it by acting on the resulting allotments.
predicates.defence_relies_on_mutual_agreement: The defending party relies on the parties’ agreement and their acts under it, rather than asking the court to decide the validity or effect of an award.

issues.definition: A defence relying on a voluntarily accepted and performed mutual division is not barred when the suit disregards that settlement and the defence does not rely on the award as such.

issues.legal_issue: A document that merely records a partition already completed by the parties does not require registration as an instrument creating rights in immovable property.
material_facts: The arbitrators’ records described property divisions that had already been made and accepted by the parties.
The parties’ acceptance and the completed divisions, rather than the records themselves, gave effect to the allotments.
Some records concerned immovable property.
issues.conclusion: The records were acknowledgments of completed partitions and were not required to be registered under section 17 of the Registration Act, 1908.
issues.legal_principle: Section 17 of the Registration Act, 1908, requires registration of specified non-testamentary instruments that themselves create, declare, assign, limit, or extinguish rights in immovable property. A record that merely acknowledges a division already completed and accepted does not itself create those rights and is not compulsorily registrable.

predicates.partition_proceeding: The court is deciding a proceeding concerning the division of property.
predicates.document_records_completed_partition: The document describes a division of property that had already been completed by the parties.
predicates.document_does_not_itself_create_property: The parties’ completed acts, rather than the document itself, created or changed their property interests.

issues.definition: A document concerning a property division need not be registered when it only records a division already completed by the parties and does not itself create property rights.

issues.legal_issue: Circumstantial evidence may establish that disputed family cash was divided even without a written record or receipts.
material_facts: A substantial amount of family cash was kept outside the family account books, and the parties knew of its existence.
Other valuable family assets were divided before lower-value items were divided.
The claimants’ pleadings did not specifically state that the cash remained undivided despite demands for its division.
A detailed list of property said to remain undivided, given to a person later asked to complete the division, did not identify the disputed cash as undivided.
Witness testimony supported the account that the cash was divided, although the Court considered the oral testimony difficult to rely on in isolation.
issues.conclusion: The Court found that the disputed family cash had been divided.
issues.legal_principle: The party asserting that a disputed asset was divided bears the burden of proving that division. The Court assessed the evidence as a whole, including the sequence of divisions, omissions from detailed pleadings and lists of undivided property, and witness testimony; the absence of a written record or receipts did not preclude the finding.

rule.if: partition_proceeding and undisclosed_family_cash and valuable_assets_divided_before_minor_items and detailed_pleadings_omit_cash_as_undivided and followup_list_omits_cash_as_undivided and witness_accounts_support_division

predicates.partition_proceeding: The court is deciding a proceeding concerning the division of family property.
predicates.undisclosed_family_cash: The family held cash outside its account books, and the parties knew that the cash existed.
predicates.valuable_assets_divided_before_minor_ite: The parties divided valuable assets before proceeding to divide comparatively low-value items.
predicates.detailed_pleadings_omit_cash_as_undivide: A party claiming that property remained undivided did not specifically identify the disputed cash as undivided in detailed pleadings.
predicates.followup_list_omits_cash_as_undivided: A party’s detailed list of property remaining to be divided did not identify the disputed cash as undivided.
predicates.witness_accounts_support_division: Witness accounts supported the claim that the disputed cash had been divided.

issues.definition: In a partition proceeding, the court may find disputed family cash divided when the surrounding sequence, detailed omissions, and supporting witness accounts collectively support that finding.

issues.legal_issue: A prior decision allocating shares does not govern property left undivided when that decision concerned only properties actually divided.
material_facts: The parties had accepted a decision allocating shares before the property was divided in stages.
Some family properties remained undivided after the accepted divisions.
The court held that the earlier share decision did not apply to the properties that had not been divided.
On the family circumstances before it, the court ordered the remaining property partitioned with one claimant receiving half and the other interests receiving one-sixth each.
issues.conclusion: The properties left undivided were to be partitioned under Hindu law, on the shares determined by the Court, rather than under the earlier allocation that applied to the divisions already made.
issues.legal_principle: Under Hindu law, property left undivided after a partial partition remains available for partition. A share decision accepted in connection with completed divisions does not automatically govern the property left undivided; the remaining property is divided consistently with the applicable rules of Hindu law.

predicates.partition_proceeding: The court is deciding a proceeding seeking division of property among family members.
predicates.property_remains_undivided: Some property remained undivided after other family property was divided.
predicates.earlier_share_decision_applied_only_to_c: The parties’ earlier share decision related to property divided under the accepted process, rather than all property held by the family.
predicates.claimant_has_half_entitlement_under_appl: The claimant’s legal relationship to the family gives the claimant a half entitlement in the remaining property under the applicable family-law rules.

issues.definition: When a partition proceeding concerns property left undivided, and the earlier share decision covered only completed divisions, the remaining property is partitioned according to the applicable family shares.
